scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The internal DNS service (BIND9) on dns_server is down, so no host can resolve web0.local–web3.local.

Mechanism: Clients’ resolvers point to 10.200.0.2 (confirmed on both hosts’ /etc/resolv.conf). DNS lookups to 10.200.0.2:53 are being actively refused, not timed out, so IP reachability is fine (pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed, and portals load via direct IP). With no process listening on UDP/TCP 53, the kernel returns “connection refused,” causing name-resolution errors.

Localization: On dns_server, there is no listener on port 53 (ss/netstat show nothing on :53) and systemd shows the DNS daemon is not running:
- systemctl status bind9: “inactive (dead)”
- ss -ltnup / netstat: no 53 listeners
On clients:
- nslookup web{0..3}.local 10.200.0.2 → “connection refused”
The BIND config itself is valid and authoritative for “local” (named-checkconf -z reports “zone local/IN: loaded”), and the zone file defines web0–web3 to 10.200.0.3–.6.

Root cause: The bind9 service on dns_server is stopped/disabled, leaving no DNS listener on port 53.

Corrective fix:
- On dns_server, start and enable the service: systemctl start bind9 && systemctl enable bind9.
- Verify it is listening: ss -ltnup | grep :53; ss -lun | grep :53.
- Re-test resolution from a host: dig web0.local @10.200.0.2 (should return 10.200.0.3).
- Optionally, ensure bind is configured to listen on all interfaces (listen-on { any; };) as already present, and keep it enabled to survive reboots. No routing issues detected elsewhere.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names and localizes the fault to dns_server (bind9/named not running and no listener on port 53).
